segments.title: Groundwork for the new components and hooks
context: This change adds a Pokemon page at /pokemon and a link to it in the header of every page. The page lists the Pokemon from the API with their level and types, and a professor can pick a trainer to list only the Pokemon of that trainer.

waypoints.title: Added `formatTypes()` to write the types of a Pokemon
waypoints.reading: The author added a function `formatTypes()` that returns the primary type of a Pokemon, or both types joined by ` / ` when it has a second type, such as `water / flying`. [`<PokemonPage />` calls it for each Pokemon of the list](code:src/routes/pokemon/index.tsx#L17), so that each line shows the types after the name and the level.

waypoints.title: Modified `<RootLayout />` to link to the Pokemon page
waypoints.reading: The author modified the component `<RootLayout />` to render a `<Link to="/pokemon">` with the text `Pokemon` in the header, between `Trainers` and `Items`. [The route table renders `<PokemonPage />` at that path](code:src/router.tsx#L14), so that a professor can open the new page from every page.

waypoints.title: Added the shape of the filter store
waypoints.reading: The author added an interface `PokemonFiltersState` with one filter, `trainerId`, which is `null` when no trainer is chosen, and the action `setTrainerId()` that changes it. [`create()` types the store with it](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#L8), so that [`<PokemonFilters />`](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L7) and [`usePokemon()`](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L8) read a typed `trainerId`.

waypoints.title: Added the Zustand store of the trainer filter
waypoints.reading:
The author added a Zustand store `usePokemonFilters` that:

- starts with `trainerId` set to `null`, so that no trainer is chosen
- sets the chosen trainer with `setTrainerId()`

[`<PokemonFilters />` writes the trainer](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L10) and [`usePokemon()` reads it](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L8), with no import between the two, so that a pick in the select changes the list the page shows.
waypoints.coreChange: This store is where the trainer filter lives. [`<PokemonFilters />`](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#PokemonFilters) writes it and [`usePokemon()`](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#usePokemon) reads it, so what `trainerId` starts at decides what the page lists when it opens.

findings.title: `usePokemonFilters` keeps the chosen trainer after the page closes
findings.reading: [`create()` makes the store once, when the module loads](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#L8), outside every component. So the chosen trainer stays set when a professor opens another page and comes back to /pokemon. Should the page open with the trainer the professor chose last, or with Every trainer?

waypoints.title: Added the union of the Pokemon type names
waypoints.reading: The author added a type `PokemonType` that is the union of the 18 Pokemon type names, from `"normal"` to `"fairy"`. [The interface `Pokemon` types `primary_type` and `secondary_type` with it](code:src/types/pokemon.ts#L9-10), so that the code that reads the types of a Pokemon gets one of these names, not any string.

waypoints.title: Added the `Pokemon` interface
waypoints.reading: The author added an interface `Pokemon` with an `id`, a `name`, a `level`, a `primary_type`, a `secondary_type` that is `null` for a Pokemon with one type, and a `trainer_id` that is `null` for a Pokemon with no trainer. The fields keep the snake_case names of the JSON the API returns, because [`request()` returns the parsed JSON as it is](code:src/api/client.ts#L19). [`fetchPokemon()` returns a list of them](code:src/api/pokemon.ts#fetchPokemon), so that the page reads each Pokemon by these names.

It also shows what happens when the user picks a trainer, and how the choice reaches the filter store.

waypoints.title: Added `fetchPokemon()` to request the Pokemon
waypoints.reading: The author added a function `fetchPokemon()` that sends a `GET` request to `/pokemon`, with `?trainer_id=` and the id when a trainer is given, and returns the Pokemon of the response. [`request()` puts `/api` in front of the path](code:src/api/client.ts#L14). [`usePokemon()` calls `fetchPokemon()` in its query function](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L11), so that the page loads only the Pokemon of the chosen trainer.

waypoints.title: Added the query key of the Pokemon
waypoints.reading: The author added a constant `POKEMON_QUERY_KEY` that holds `["pokemon"]`. [`usePokemon()` adds the chosen trainer to it](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L10), so that each trainer has its own cached list and a new trainer loads the list again.

waypoints.title: Added `usePokemon()` to load the Pokemon of the chosen trainer
waypoints.reading:
The author added a hook `usePokemon()` that:

- reads `trainerId` from [the filter store](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#usePokemonFilters)
- loads the Pokemon of that trainer with [`fetchPokemon()`](code:src/api/pokemon.ts#fetchPokemon), under a key that holds the trainer

[`<PokemonPage />` calls it with no argument](code:src/routes/pokemon/index.tsx#L6), so that the list follows [the trainer select](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L10) with no prop between the select and the page.
waypoints.coreChange: This is where the trainer filter reaches the data: `trainerId` from [the filter store](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#usePokemonFilters) goes into the query key and into the request. The page, the select and the store all exist for it.

children.title: Added the read of the chosen trainer
children.reading: The author added a call to [`usePokemonFilters()`](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#usePokemonFilters) with a selector that returns `trainerId`. The hook renders again only when the trainer changes, and [the query key holds the trainer](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L10).

children.title: Added the query of the Pokemon
children.reading: The author added a call to `useQuery` with the key `["pokemon", 3]` for the trainer with id 3, or `["pokemon", null]` for Every trainer, and a query function that calls [`fetchPokemon()`](code:src/api/pokemon.ts#fetchPokemon) with the same trainer. A new trainer is a new key, so `useQuery` requests the list again, and [`<PokemonPage />` reads the result](code:src/routes/pokemon/index.tsx#L6).

findings.title: `usePokemon()` empties the list for a trainer it has not loaded yet
findings.reading: [The query key holds `trainerId`](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L10), so a trainer with no cached list starts a new query with no data. While it loads, `isPending` is `true` and `data` is `undefined`, so [the page shows `Loading the Pokemon…`](code:src/routes/pokemon/index.tsx#L11) and [no list](code:src/routes/pokemon/index.tsx#L13). `placeholderData: keepPreviousData` from `@tanstack/react-query` keeps the last list on screen until the new one arrives, for one more option. The fix also imports `keepPreviousData` on [the first line of the file](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L1).

waypoints.title: Modified the route table to add the Pokemon page
waypoints.reading: The author modified the route table `router` to add a child route `pokemon` of the layout that renders [`<PokemonPage />`](code:src/routes/pokemon/index.tsx#PokemonPage). `src/main.tsx` passes this table to `<RouterProvider />`, so that the page opens at `/pokemon` inside [`<RootLayout />`](code:src/routes/root-layout.tsx#RootLayout), where [the header links to it](code:src/routes/root-layout.tsx#L11).

waypoints.title: Added the value of the Every trainer option
waypoints.reading: The author added a constant `EVERY` that holds `""`. [The trainer select uses it as the value of its first option, `Every trainer`](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L11), and [its handler calls `setTrainerId(null)` when that option is picked](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L10). So the store holds `null` for Every trainer and never `""`, and [`fetchPokemon()` sends no `trainer_id` for `null`](code:src/api/pokemon.ts#L5).

waypoints.title: Added `<PokemonFilters />` to pick a trainer
waypoints.reading:
The author added a component `<PokemonFilters />` that:

- renders a select with `Every trainer` and one option per trainer from [`useTrainers()`](code:src/hooks/use-trainers.ts#L6-8)
- shows the trainer of [the filter store](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#usePokemonFilters) as the picked option
- writes each pick to the store with [`setTrainerId()`](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#L10-12)

[`<PokemonPage />` renders it above the list](code:src/routes/pokemon/index.tsx#L10), so that a professor can narrow the list to one trainer.

children.title: Added the read of the filter store
children.reading: The author added a call to [`usePokemonFilters()`](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#usePokemonFilters) with no selector, which returns the whole store: `trainerId` and `setTrainerId()`. [The select shows `trainerId` as its value](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L10), and [its handler calls `setTrainerId()`](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L10).

children.title: Added the query of the trainers
children.reading: The author added a call to [`useTrainers()`](code:src/hooks/use-trainers.ts#L6-8) that gives the loaded trainers, with `[]` until they arrive. [The select renders one option per trainer](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L12-16), so the select offers only `Every trainer` while the trainers load.

findings.title: `<PokemonFilters />` hides a failed load of the trainers
findings.reading: [`useTrainers()` reports a failed request in `isError`](code:src/hooks/use-trainers.ts#L7), and `<PokemonFilters />` reads only `data`, with `[]` in its place. So when the trainers do not load, [the select offers `Every trainer` alone](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L10-17), and nothing tells the professor why. The fix reads `isError` here, and [the select](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L10-17) then needs a message for `hasTrainerError`.
trace: [The select renders `Every trainer` and no other option](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L10-17).
findings.solution: const { data: trainers = [], isError: hasTrainerError } = useTrainers()

children.title: Added the handler of the trainer select
children.reading: The author added an `onChange` handler that calls [`setTrainerId(3)`](code:src/stores/pokemon-filters.ts#L10-12) when a professor picks the trainer with id 3, and `setTrainerId(null)` when the picked value is [`EVERY`](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#EVERY). [`usePokemon()` puts the trainer in its query key](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#L10), so that the page requests the Pokemon of that trainer.

children.title: Added one option per trainer
children.reading: The author added a loop that renders one `<option>` per trainer, with the `id` as its value and the `name` as its text. [The handler of the select turns the value back into a number](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#L10), so that the store holds the id as a number.

waypoints.title: Added `<PokemonPage />` to list the Pokemon
waypoints.reading:
The author added a page component `<PokemonPage />` that:

- renders the heading `Pokemon` and [`<PokemonFilters />`](code:src/routes/pokemon/components/PokemonFilters.tsx#PokemonFilters)
- loads the Pokemon of the chosen trainer with [`usePokemon()`](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#usePokemon)
- shows `Loading the Pokemon…` while they load, and `The Pokemon could not be loaded.` when the request fails
- renders one line per Pokemon with its name, its level and [its types](code:src/lib/format.ts#formatTypes)

[The route table renders it at `/pokemon`](code:src/router.tsx#L14), and [the header links to it](code:src/routes/root-layout.tsx#L11), so that a professor can browse the Pokemon.

children.title: Added the read of the Pokemon query
children.reading: The author added a call to [`usePokemon()`](code:src/hooks/use-pokemon.ts#usePokemon) that gives the Pokemon of the chosen trainer as `pokemon`, and the flags `isPending` and `isError`. [The three conditions below read them](code:src/routes/pokemon/index.tsx#L11-13).

children.title: Added the loading message of the Pokemon list
children.reading:
The author added a condition that renders `

Loading the Pokemon…

` while the query is pending. [The trainer select stays above it](code:src/routes/pokemon/index.tsx#L10), so a professor can pick another trainer while the list loads.

children.title: Added the error message of the Pokemon list
children.reading:
The author added a condition that renders `

The Pokemon could not be loaded.

` when the query fails, as it does when [`request()` throws an `ApiError`](code:src/api/client.ts#L18), so that a failed request shows a message in place of the list.

children.title: Added the list of the Pokemon
children.reading: The author added a condition that renders a `<ul>` once the Pokemon have loaded, with one `<li>` per Pokemon that shows its name, `Lv.` and its level, and the text of [`formatTypes()`](code:src/lib/format.ts#formatTypes).

findings.title: `<PokemonPage />` renders an empty list when the trainer has no Pokemon
findings.reading: When the API returns `[]` for the chosen trainer, [`fetchPokemon()` returns it as it is](code:src/api/pokemon.ts#L6). `[]` is truthy, so the condition renders an empty `<ul>`, and the professor sees the select with nothing under it. A message for an empty list says that there is no Pokemon to show, for one more condition.
